relevance_note: Single-patient case report of a person with a diagnosis of Alexander disease (in scope by diagnosis): "MRI diagnosis of infantile Alexander disease in a 14 month old African boy"; no GFAP variant is reported for him.
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a short Python script only assembled the JSON. One in-scope person, labelled 'patient' (rule 5). The diagnosis was made on MRI criteria; the paper reports no genetic testing and no GFAP variant for this patient, so the variants table is empty and n_patients_reported is null (no patient with a stated GFAP variant). The converted Case Report section is out of order (the MRI paragraph is split across two '## CASE REPORT' blocks: one ends 'with extension to the anterior temporal lobes and have requested a repeat MRI scan', the other begins mid-sentence 'occipital lobes'); no span joins text across these breaks. 14 months is the age at referral/MRI diagnosis, recorded as age at diagnosis; age at last evaluation left 'not reported' to avoid duplicating it. Vital status 'alive' rests on 'currently being managed'. 'he was feeding well' recorded as feeding difficulties excluded, but the checklist item dysphagia left 'not reported'. 'The brainstem was normal' recorded as excluded brainstem abnormality, but the composite checklist item 'medulla or cervical spinal cord atrophy or signal abnormality' left 'not reported' (cervical cord not addressed). Tables 1 and 2 and the Discussion are general disease summaries with no individual-level data; previously published patients are cited only by reference number, so no literature rows. No contradictions found. HPO IDs are candidates only.
